name: NVIDIA
thesis: Dominant AI GPU provider powering the datacenter buildout. Blackwell architecture driving unprecedented demand. Data center 80%+ of revenue.

name: AMD
thesis: AMD has emerged as the credible #2 AI accelerator vendor with ~12 GW of multi-year committed deployments — ~$100B from OpenAI's 6 GW partnership (with up to 160M warrant shares vesting on milestones) and ~$60B from Meta's expanded 6 GW deal — both anchored by the MI450 Instinct ramp starting H2 2026 alongside sixth-gen 'Venice' EPYC CPUs. Q1 2026 datacenter revenue of $5.8B (+57% YoY) and Q2 guidance of $11.2B (+46% YoY) validate Instinct share gains; the pivotal upside mechanism is converting contracted gigawatts into recurring high-margin GPU revenue while NVIDIA's CUDA stack remains the incumbent moat to overcome.

name: Broadcom
thesis: Custom AI ASIC leader (Google TPU, Meta MTIA). Networking infrastructure critical for datacenter interconnect.

name: Intel
thesis: Turnaround play with Gaudi AI accelerators and 18A process node. Foundry services ambitions. CHIPS Act beneficiary.

name: Micron Technology
thesis: HBM leader benefiting from AI GPU memory demand. HBM3E supply sold out through 2025-2026.
catalysts: AI-driven memory content increase per server

name: SK Hynix
thesis: Leading HBM manufacturer and NVIDIA's primary HBM supplier. HBM3E production leader with strong pricing power.
note: US ADR SKHY on Nasdaq since 2026-07-10 (verified Yahoo 2026-10-02). Prefer SKHY for Fidelity.

name: Samsung Electronics
thesis: World's largest memory manufacturer catching up in HBM. Foundry + memory combination unique in industry.
risks: HBM quality gap vs SK Hynix

name: Arista Networks
thesis: Dominant AI datacenter networking franchise. Surpassed Cisco in datacenter switching market share. AI networking target raised to $3.5B. Post-earnings pullback may be buying opportunity.

name: Cisco Systems
thesis: Networking giant with Splunk acquisition expanding AI observability. Silicon One chips for AI datacenter fabric.

name: Amphenol
thesis: High-quality electrical connector compounder with exceptional datacom growth. Q1 2026 revenue +49% YoY.

name: Corning
thesis: NVIDIA $3.2B partnership positions Corning at center of optical AI infrastructure. 10x US optical manufacturing expansion, 50%+ fiber capacity increase.

name: Super Micro Computer
thesis: Leading AI server/rack manufacturer with direct liquid cooling. Building Block architecture for rapid custom configurations.

name: Dell Technologies
thesis: Leading AI server OEM with PowerEdge platform. Infrastructure Solutions Group driving growth from enterprise AI deployments.

name: HPE
thesis: Enterprise AI infrastructure provider with Juniper Networks acquisition expanding networking portfolio.

name: Celestica
thesis: Pure-play datacenter hardware manufacturer. 1.6T networking platform. $17B 2026E revenue guidance (+37%).

name: Vertiv
thesis: Dominant datacenter thermal management and power distribution leader riding the AI infrastructure supercycle. Q1 2026 revenue $2.65B (+30% YoY) with adjusted EPS of $1.17 (+83% YoY). FY2025 revenue reached $10.2B (+28% YoY) with $1.3B net income (+169%). Backlog surged to $15.0B (+109% YoY) with Q4 2025 book-to-bill of 2.9x driven by 252% organic orders growth. Adjusted operating margin expanded to 20.8% in Q1 2026 (+430bps YoY). Raised 2026 guidance to $13.5-14.0B revenue (+34% growth) with adj. EPS of $6.30-6.40 (+51%). Net leverage at 0.2x with $5.0B liquidity. CoolPhase Flex hybrid cooling and 800VDC power solutions position Vertiv at the center of the liquid cooling transition for 100+ kW AI racks.
catalysts: $15.0B backlog (+109% YoY) with book-to-bill of 2.9x — orders accelerating, not decelerating
2026 guidance raised to $13.5-14.0B revenue (+34% growth), adj. EPS $6.30-6.40 (+51%)
Q1 2026 adjusted free cash flow $653M (+147% YoY) — cash generation inflecting sharply
Liquid cooling supercycle: CoolPhase Flex and 800VDC solutions for NVIDIA next-gen GPU racks
Adjusted operating margin expansion to 22.8-23.8% guided for FY2026 (+290bps vs FY2025)
risks: Premium valuation at ~42x forward P/E and $131B market cap — priced for perfection
Hyperscaler customer concentration — top customers drive outsized revenue share
Execution risk on 34% revenue growth with simultaneous margin expansion
STL acquisition integration risk alongside organic growth demands
Potential demand moderation if hyperscaler capex cycle decelerates

name: Asetek
thesis: Liquid cooling specialist for AI datacenters. Direct-to-chip and rear-door heat exchanger solutions.
catalysts: AI GPU power density driving demand
note: Was Nasdaq Copenhagen ASTK. CQXA takeover completed Apr 2026; last trading day 2026-05-21; now private. Older Oslo-2024 delisting note obsolete.
